title: Runtime diagnostic decision tree and observability onramp for error-class enrichment
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Problem: on-call and platform teams lack a deterministic, low-noise way to map surface signals (timeouts, gRPC/HTTP codes, model-run errors, throttle responses) to a small set of actionable failure classes. Current dashboards scatter these signals across traces, logs, and raw metrics which increases mean time to detect and remediate runtime degradations.

Goal: build a diagnostic decision tree and an 'observability onramp' that enriches traces and logs with a canonical failure_class, overload_score, and model_reject_signature at ingestion time; wire these fields into a small set of error-first dashboards and alert conditions. The product should: (1) standardize classification rules across runtime, API gateway, and model adapters, (2) reduce noise by grouping similar root causes (e.g., kernel OOM vs request-level overload vs model rejection), and (3) provide drilldown links to raw trace spans, sampled request logs, and candidate rollback/mitigation playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing ingestion pipeline adds canonical fields: failure_class, failure_subtype, overload_score, model_signature for 95% of requests within realtime window
Failure taxonomy documented and agreed by infra, runtime, and platform SREs (document link added to design_links)
Three dashboards created: Error Overview (high-level), Overload & Backpressure Explorer, Model Rejection Lens; each supports time-range, service, and route filters
Alert rules updated to use failure_class with reduced noise (target: reduce false-positive alerts by 30%)
Playbook links surfaced from dashboard rows for top-10 most frequent failure signatures
Validated end-to-end with synthetic traffic that exercises timeouts, gRPC codes (UNAVAILABLE, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED), rate-limited responses, kernel OOM traces, and model-run exceptions
tasks: Define canonical failure taxonomy and mapping table (team workshop)
Implement tracehook enrichment to attach failure_class at span close for sampled traces
Add log-shipper enrichment rules to append failure_class/failure_subtype for full logs
Extend metrics pipeline to emit overload_score histogram and per-route failure_class counters
Create three Grafana/Console dashboards and low-cardinality tiles for alerts
Run integration test with staging load generator and compare classification labels against golden dataset
Rollout: canary to 10% of runtime nodes, monitor classification drift, then 100%
dashboards: Error Overview — failure_class heatmap by service and route
Overload & Backpressure Explorer — overload_score distribution, backpressure provenance
Model Rejection Lens — model_signature patterns, prompt slices, rejection counts
rollout_plan: Deploy tracehook enrichment in two phases: phase 1 (canary 10%): enrich sampled traces and logs with failure_class but do not change alerts; phase 2 (full): enable new dashboards and swap alert rules to rely on failure_class. Each phase monitored for 72 hours with explicit rollback criteria: classification drift > 10% vs golden set or alert noise increases.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for mapping table and enrichment logic. 2) Integration job that replays 10k synthetic requests covering all taxonomy branches and validates produced failure_class equals expected. 3) Canary monitoring: manual review of top-50 signatures, automated comparison to golden dataset.
